channel.title: Theraglee challenges
channel.description: Daily wellbeing challenge themes from Theraglee, two new ones a day.

item.title: Welcoming People into Your Home
item.description: For anyone who would like to have people over more often but feels the house, the cooking or the nerves get in the way. Each day is one small step toward simple, low key hospitality, from a cup of tea with a neighbor to a relaxed potluck.

item.title: Taming the Paperwork Pile
item.description: For anyone whose mail, forms, bills and important papers have turned into a pile they avoid. Each day is one small, doable step toward knowing where things are, keeping up with what comes in and feeling calmer about it.

item.title: Getting Back to a Hobby You Loved
item.description: For anyone who has let a favorite pastime slip away under work, family or a busy season. Each day is one small step back toward it, from dusting off the gear to finding ten minutes and enjoying being a little rusty.

item.title: Finding Meaning in Your Work
item.description: For anyone whose work, paid or unpaid, has started to feel like just a list of tasks. Each day is one small way to notice who your work helps, take pride in doing it well and connect it to what you care about.

item.title: Settling Into a New Place
item.description: For anyone who has moved recently, or who still does not quite feel at home where they live. Each day is one small way to make your space your own, learn your neighborhood and find your people.

item.title: Writing Letters and Little Notes
item.description: For anyone who misses the warmth of a handwritten word. Each day is one small way to write a note, card or letter, to the people around you, to faraway friends or to yourself, and let it say what matters.

item.title: Trusting Yourself More
item.description: For anyone who second-guesses every choice or checks with everyone else before deciding. Each day is one small way to notice your own good sense, keep promises to yourself and let your judgment count.

item.title: Making Days Off Feel Restful
item.description: For anyone whose weekends or days off vanish into errands, catch-up work and screens. Each day is one small way to slow down, leave work behind and make your time off feel like time that is yours.

item.title: Being Present with Your Kids
item.description: For any parent, grandparent or caregiver who wants more unhurried moments with the children in their life, from toddlers to teens. Each day is one small way to put distractions down and simply be with them.

item.title: Handling Rejection Gently
item.description: For anyone who takes a no hard, whether it comes from a job, a date, a friend or a group. Each day is one small way to steady yourself, keep it in proportion and keep reaching for what matters.

item.title: Cheering Other People On
item.description: For anyone who wants to be the friend, coworker and neighbor who notices good news and celebrates it. Each day is one small way to cheer someone on, even when their success stings a little.

item.title: Bouncing Back from Mistakes
item.description: For anyone who replays every slip for days afterward. Each day is one small way to meet a mistake calmly, put right what you can, learn from it and let the rest go.

item.title: Staying Informed Without the Overwhelm
item.description: For anyone who feels drained or on edge from the headlines. Each day is one small way to follow the news on your own terms, stay caring and informed, and step back when it gets heavy.

item.title: Growing Older Gently
item.description: For anyone, at any age, who feels uneasy about the years adding up. Each day is one small way to meet getting older with kindness, curiosity and appreciation for the life you have lived so far.

item.title: Feeling at Home in Your Body
item.description: For anyone who feels at odds with their body or only notices it when something hurts. Each day is one small way to notice, thank and care for it, so your body feels more like a friendly place to live.

item.title: Staying Curious
item.description: For anyone whose days have started to feel flat or stuck on autopilot. Each day is one small way to wonder, ask and notice, so ordinary life and the people in it feel a little more interesting.

item.title: Being Kind Online
item.description: For anyone who wants their time on screens to feel friendlier. Each day is one small way to bring warmth and care to messages, comments and group chats, from a sincere compliment to pausing before a heated reply.

item.title: Breathing a Little Easier
item.description: For anyone who notices they hold their breath or breathe fast when life gets busy. Each day is one short, gentle breathing practice, a few slow breaths at a desk, in a line or at bedtime, so calm has an easy way in.

item.title: Laughing More Often
item.description: For anyone who can't remember the last time they laughed out loud. Each day is one small way to invite more humor and lightness in, from a silly video shared with a friend to noticing the funny side of a small mishap.

item.title: Loosening Old Grudges
item.description: For anyone still carrying anger about something that happened a while ago. Each day is one small step toward setting it down for your own sake, at your own pace, without having to excuse what happened or reconnect with anyone.

item.title: Planning Small Adventures
item.description: For anyone whose weeks have started to look the same. Each day is one small step toward a little adventure close to home, from a new street to walk to a day trip you finally plan, so ordinary life gets a spark of something new.

item.title: Getting Through a Hard Day
item.description: For anyone facing a day that feels heavy, long or simply too much. Each day is one small, steadying thing to do in the middle of it, from a glass of water to one honest text, so a hard day gets a little more bearable.

item.title: Making Room for Quiet
item.description: For anyone whose days are full of noise, screens and chatter. Each day is one small way to find a pocket of quiet, from a silent first sip of coffee to a walk without headphones, so your mind gets a little room to settle.

item.title: Letting Kindness In
item.description: For anyone who is quick to help others but brushes off compliments, offers and thanks. Each day is one small practice in receiving: saying a simple thank you, accepting a hand, and letting care from other people land.

item.title: Growing Something Green
item.description: For anyone who would like a little more life around them, with or without a yard. Each day is one small step in growing plants, from a windowsill herb to a community garden plot, so tending something living becomes a quiet daily pleasure.

item.title: Finding Patience in Everyday Waiting
item.description: For anyone who gets wound up in lines, on hold or stuck behind a slow driver. Each day is one small way to turn waiting into a calmer moment, so delays sting a little less and the rest of the day goes more smoothly.

item.title: Keeping a Simple Journal
item.description: For anyone who would like to write things down but never knows where to start. Each day is one short prompt or page habit, a few lines in a notebook or on your phone, to sort your thoughts, remember good moments and know yourself a little better.

item.title: Starting Conversations with Strangers
item.description: For anyone who would like a little more friendly contact in daily life. Each day is one small, low-stakes way to say hello, ask a question or share a kind word with someone you don't know, from a cashier to a neighbor at the bus stop.

item.title: Enjoying Time with Animals
item.description: For anyone who feels lighter around pets, birds or wildlife. Each day is one small way to notice, care for or simply spend time with animals, from watching birds at a feeder to a slow walk with a dog.

item.title: Making Home Feel Cozy
item.description: For anyone whose home feels more like a place to pass through than a place to rest. Each day is one small, low-cost change to light, comfort, sound or color that makes coming home feel warmer.

item.title: Handling Conflict at Work
item.description: For anyone who dreads a tense coworker, a prickly email or a disagreement in a meeting. Each day is one small, practical step toward calmer, clearer conversations at work, so disagreements get settled instead of stewing.

item.title: Making Music Part of Your Day
item.description: For anyone who has let music fade into the background. Each day is one small way to listen, sing, play or move to music on purpose, so it can lift a mood, settle a busy mind or bring people together.

item.title: Cooking for Yourself
item.description: For anyone who lives on takeout, snacks or skipped meals and would like more home-cooked comfort. Each day is one small, low-pressure kitchen step, from stocking a staple to cooking one simple dish, so feeding yourself feels doable and kind.

item.title: Getting Along Better with Family
item.description: For anyone who loves their family but finds time together tense or tiring. Each day is one small step toward easier conversations, kinder visits and calmer limits, whether your family lives under your roof or across the country.

item.title: Leaving Work at Work
item.description: For anyone whose job follows them home in their head, their inbox or their evenings. Each day is one small step that closes the workday on purpose, so your evenings and weekends feel like your own again.

item.title: Reading for Pleasure
item.description: For anyone who used to love books but lost the habit somewhere along the way. Each day is one small step back toward reading for fun, from a single page at breakfast to a library visit, with no reading list to finish.

item.title: Making Something with Your Hands
item.description: For anyone whose days happen mostly on screens. Each day is one small hands-on making task, from folding, sketching and mending to baking or potting a plant, done for the pleasure of making rather than for a perfect result.

item.title: Studying Without the Stress
item.description: For students and lifelong learners who dread the books. Each day is one small study habit, from a short focused session to a tidy desk or a practice question, that makes learning steadier and the night before a test calmer.

item.title: Making Peace with Uncertainty
item.description: For anyone who finds not knowing harder than bad news. Each day is one small practice in acting without every answer, loosening the need for certainty, and noticing how often things work out in ways you could not have planned.

item.title: Taking Care of Future You
item.description: For anyone who keeps leaving tomorrow's problems for tomorrow's tired self. Each day is one small kindness done now that your future self will thank you for, from a filled water bottle to a booked appointment.

item.title: Living Less Rushed
item.description: For anyone who hurries through everything, even when there is no real deadline. Each day is one small way to build in a little extra time, slow one ordinary activity down, and notice that most things go fine at an easier pace.

item.title: Giving Back to Your Community
item.description: For anyone who would like to help out beyond their own four walls but is not sure where to start. Each day is one small, doable way to give some time, skill or care to the community around you, at whatever scale fits your life.

item.title: Easing Sunday Night Dread
item.description: For anyone whose weekend ends with a knot in the stomach about the week ahead. Each day is one small way to prepare gently, keep the last evening of the weekend your own, and start the week with less dread.

item.title: Showing Up for a Friend
item.description: For anyone who wants to be there for the people they care about, especially when life gets hard for them. Each day is one small, practical way to check in, listen, help, or celebrate, so friends feel less alone.

item.title: Taking Real Breaks at Work
item.description: For anyone who eats lunch at the desk, skips breaks, and reaches the end of the workday drained. Each day is one small way to step away, reset your body and mind, and come back clearer, whatever kind of work you do.

item.title: Speaking Up in Groups
item.description: For anyone who has something to say in a meeting, class or group conversation and stays quiet. Each day is one small, low-stakes step toward sharing a thought, asking a question, or disagreeing kindly, so your voice gets heard.

item.title: Easing Holiday Stress
item.description: For anyone who loves the holidays and still finds them exhausting, or dreads them outright. Each day is one small way to plan, pace, and protect your energy through gatherings, travel, spending and family expectations, so the season has more room for what matters to you.

item.title: Steadying Yourself Through Change
item.description: For anyone going through a move, a new job, a breakup, a new baby, retirement or any big shift. Each day is one small way to find steady ground, keep a few anchors in place, and give yourself time to adjust.

item.title: Comparing Yourself Less
item.description: For anyone who measures their life against other people's highlights and comes up short. Each day is one small practice in noticing the comparison, stepping out of it, and coming back to your own pace, values and progress.

item.title: Being Kinder with Your Partner
item.description: For couples who love each other and still slip into snapping, scorekeeping or taking each other for granted. Each day is one small, kind thing to say or do for your partner, so warmth gets a regular place in the everyday.
